chapter: New York, Dallas and Kansas City
title: Arriving in New York and the Rhythm Club, joining Local 802
summary: Moore bought a bus ticket to New York, hung around the Rhythm Club among famous musicians, and joined the union; he then took a job in Newark.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Those are later years, yeh Okay, let's see, how did you end up in New York?

Well, we'll start from Celestin. From Dothan, Alabama, I left the band when my money came from my land in Arizona, and I bought a bus ticket clear to New York. When I got into New York I asked where the musicians hang out. Naturally I asked the black musicians say, well, they always hang out at the Rhythm Club, that's around 140th and 7th Avenue. So here I am up in the Rhythm Club, I got me a hotel, I'm hanging around, and I see famous musicians there but I was reluctant to form an acquaintance because they don't know me -- I know them, like Jeilly Roll Morton and all them famous names, I was agasp about meeting such important great musicians. I'd just stay there practically the whole day just looking at them because they usually

sleep late and they and they come around around 3, 4, 5 o'clock in the afternoon and they all congregate in the River Club, famous names of bands from the Savoy Ballroom -- Claude Hopkins, Chick Webb, Savoy Sultans, Lucky Millinder, Cecil Scott had a group there at the Savoy, all the bands that ever played there, all them guys hang around there. Some faces looked familiar and then some faces are famous. I met one or two guys that I used to remember on the road. I met Claude Hopkins in Dallas, while I was in Dallas and I met some of the musicians, and some of the musicians -- Andy Kirk was there. Some of the guys from Ellington. I got acquainted all over again and talked about conditions, getting gigs, and they said, put your card into the Union -- 802.
Did you join the union right away?
Yes, I joined the union and I didn't get any work right away, but I had to move to Newark, New Jersey, because I had a little job there at the Bluebird Dance Hall on Market Street in Newark.
Yes, all the bands would come through the Paramount in Newark, like Larry Clinton, Glenn Miller, Basie and all them fine guys, wishing I could be in the band, you know, I'm dreaming, fantasizing.

and I was staying at a hotel near the big post office in Newark and near Chinatown, I ate my Chinese food there and go to my little job, playing at the 10¢ a dance thing, this is '39. That was the same year when I left Celestin in Dothan, Alabama.
